reasons: Party mapping is correct: HDI is the vendor (designs, develops, hosts the Site) and the Company (our alias) is the customer, so an ownership clause in our favour is directionally right.

The finding is genuinely 'missing': the cited paragraphs (1.1 development, 2.1 Content delivery, 5.2 artistic/editorial control, 6.1 trademark licence, 7.1 e-mail lists) contain no ownership or assignment allocation, and §10.2's no-partnership co-ownership disclaimer is not an IP allocation.

The inserted §5.5 reaches the preferred position with a single additive clause: Company ownership of Content, Marks and customer/transaction data with no assignment to HDI; HDI assignment of the Site and other Deliverables; HDI retention of pre-existing platform/tools with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back to embedded HDI Materials; and an express no-joint-ownership sentence. Nothing in the original text is deleted or distorted.

No walk-away trigger is created (no assignment of Customer IP/data to HDI, no joint ownership), and the data-ownership sentence does not conflict with the reciprocal e-mail list use rights in §7.1, which remain intact.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position and offers the licence-back fallback if HDI resists the assignment; deterministic checks both pass.

Minor, non-disqualifying risk: the clause is appended to p0035 as '5.5' and the surrounding numbering (the fragment appears to be 5.3/5.4) is not fully visible, so the section number should be confirmed against the executed numbering before sending.
